items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to notification of death of inmates to next of kin
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S5427               REVISED 1/7/16

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the correction law, in relation to
notification of death of inmates to next of kin

 PURPOSE :  This bill would require the department of corrections and
community supervision (DOCCS) to be responsive to the next of kin or
other designated person who inquire as to the circumstances
surrounding the death of a prisoner, and to provide such person with
an original preliminary death certificate

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section one of the bill amends section 47 of the correction law to
require the State Commission of Correction (SCOC) to be responsive to
inquiries from family members or designated representatives who
contact the SCOC regarding the circumstances that led to the death of
their loved one. SCOC is statutorily required to conduct
investigations into inmate deaths with the goal of improving policy in
order to avoid similar deaths in the future. SCOC investigations begin
after the coroner and state police have completed their medical and
criminal investigations.

Section two of the bill adds a new section 624 to the correction law
requiring the Department of Corrections and Community
Supervision(DOCCS) to be responsive to inquiries from family members
or designated representatives regarding the death of their loved ones.
DOCCS may relay the circumstances surrounding the death of the inmate,
medical procedures used and preliminary cause of death determinations.

Section three amends section 16 of the correction law to require DOCCS
to acquire a preliminary or final death certificate from the issuing
coroner or medical examiner and forward such original death
certificate to the inmate's next of kin.

Section four of the bill is the effective date.

 JUSTIFICATION :  Every incarcerated individual is someone's son or
daughter, father or mother, brother or sister. Every year
approximately 150 inmates die while in the care, custody and control
of the Department of Corrections and Community Supervision (DOCCS).
They may have been surprisingly young or very old, may have had mental
illness or died from medical conditions for which they were being
treated prior to incarceration, or may have died from circumstances
that were seemingly preventable or foreseeable.

Most die from natural causes, a term which includes death by injury
sustained in a fight or assault, complications from medical
conditions, overdose, heart attacks, and more. Sadly, between 10 and
20 incarcerated individuals typically die each year from suicide.

When an inmate has died, outside hospitals and county coroners are
responsive only to DOCCS and routinely tell next of kin that they must
contact the facility where the inmate had been in custody. At the same
time the facility employees will refer the next of kin back to the
hospital or coroner. The State Commission of Correction which
investigates the deaths of incarcerated individuals does not begin its
investigation until after the coroner and the state police
investigations have been completed. SCOC investigations are often not
complete until 12-18 months after an incarcerated individual's deaths,
a very long time to wait for information when someone in your family
has died in custody.

Close family members like parents, spouses and children should be able
to find out what their loved one died from when being told how to
retrieve the body, and they should receive a preliminary death
certificate at the earliest opportunity. We have received testimony at
public hearings, calls and letters from parents of inmate suicide
victims telling us that obtaining such information is very difficult.
The intent of this bill is to help make a difficult situation easier
to navigate.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY : New Bill

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS : None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :  This act shall take effect on the one hundred
twentieth day after it shall have become a law. Effective immediately,
the addition, amendment and/or repeal of any rules or regulations
necessary for the implementation of the foregoing section of this act
on its effective date is authorized to be made on or before such
effective date.
